forces.title: Growing hotel occupancy drives new premium room additions
forces.description: India’s hotel occupancies are projected to experience a spurt, with a CAGR of 3.5-4%, leading to the addition of approximately 15,000-16,000 premium branded rooms. This expansion signifies increased development and ownership opportunities in hotel real estate, as operators expand their physical asset base to meet rising demand. This is relevant for property owners or developers in the hospitality sector, even if no listed Hotel REITs currently exist in India.

demand_drivers.description: Global investors, including foreign sponsors, pension pools, sovereign entities, and institutional Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), form the backbone of the unitholder mix for InvITs, holding approximately 55% of units.
The rapid institutionalisation of operational infrastructure platforms in India, leveraging investment vehicles like InvITs, drives the growth of Assets Under Management.

new_opportunities.description: The heavy concentration of InvIT AUM in telecom and roads (accounting for nearly 90%) signals significant untapped opportunities for diversification into other asset classes beyond these two segments, potentially including other specialty real estate categories.

market_sizing.methodology: Assets Under Management (AUM) for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), with telecom representing a concentrated primary segment alongside roads. This figure represents the investment in telecom infrastructure assets held by InvITs.
